attr_definition: How the agent opens the call. Covers use of the approved Runaki opening script, clear identification of self and of Runaki, and the professionalism and warmth of the first 10-15 seconds, delivered in the language the customer opens in (Arabic, Sorani or Badini).
reason: Pass
definition: Full pass. The agent delivers the complete approved opening within the first few seconds, identifies Runaki and themselves by name, invites the customer to speak, and sounds warm, clear and ready to help.
pass_example: "Good morning, thank you for calling Runaki, my name is Dilan. How may I help you today?" - delivered clearly and warmly, in the language the customer used.

attr_definition: How the agent opens the call. Covers use of the approved Runaki opening script, clear identification of self and of Runaki, and the professionalism and warmth of the first 10-15 seconds, delivered in the language the customer opens in (Arabic, Sorani or Badini).
reason: Did not use the approved opening greeting / script
definition: The agent opened the call but the wording departed from the approved script - the branded welcome, the time-of-day greeting or the offer of assistance was missing or reworded. The customer is still greeted and knows the call has been answered, so this scores 2 rather than 1.
pass_example: Agent uses the approved wording in full and in the correct order, with no elements dropped or improvised.

attr_definition: How the agent opens the call. Covers use of the approved Runaki opening script, clear identification of self and of Runaki, and the professionalism and warmth of the first 10-15 seconds, delivered in the language the customer opens in (Arabic, Sorani or Badini).
reason: Did not introduce self and/or Runaki clearly
definition: The customer cannot tell who they are speaking to or which organisation they have reached. Applies where the agent's name, the Runaki brand name, or both, are omitted, mumbled, or delivered too fast to be understood.
pass_example: "Thank you for calling Runaki, this is Ahmed speaking." - both the brand and the agent name are audible and distinct.

attr_definition: How the agent opens the call. Covers use of the approved Runaki opening script, clear identification of self and of Runaki, and the professionalism and warmth of the first 10-15 seconds, delivered in the language the customer opens in (Arabic, Sorani or Badini).
reason: Tone at call start was flat, rushed or unwelcoming
definition: The approved words may be present but the delivery is not. The greeting is read at speed, monotone, sighing or audibly disengaged, setting a negative tone before the customer has said anything.
pass_example: Greeting delivered at a steady pace with an audible smile, so the customer starts speaking without hesitation.

attr_definition: How the agent opens the call. Covers use of the approved Runaki opening script, clear identification of self and of Runaki, and the professionalism and warmth of the first 10-15 seconds, delivered in the language the customer opens in (Arabic, Sorani or Badini).
reason: Call opening was not professional or confident
definition: The opening undermines customer confidence: long dead air before speaking, background noise or side conversation on the floor, eating or drinking, casual slang, or stumbling and self-correcting through the script.
pass_example: Agent answers promptly from a quiet line and opens confidently, with no hesitation, background noise or false starts.

attr_definition: Correctly establishing who the caller is and which account, meter or location the enquiry relates to. Covers capturing every identifier required by the Runaki process (name, area/address, contact number, subscriber/meter or complaint reference), working in the correct record, and reading details back for confirmation before acting on them.
reason: Pass
definition: Full pass. All identifiers required by the Runaki process are requested in a logical order, captured accurately, confirmed back to the customer, and the agent is demonstrably working in the correct record.
pass_example: "May I take your full name, please? And which area? Thank you - so that is Rebin Othman, Ainkawa, Account Number X. Is that correct?"

attr_definition: Correctly establishing who the caller is and which account, meter or location the enquiry relates to. Covers capturing every identifier required by the Runaki process (name, area/address, contact number, subscriber/meter or complaint reference), working in the correct record, and reading details back for confirmation before acting on them.
reason: Verified the customer's name but not the location, or vice versa.
definition: Partial verification. One core identifier is captured and confirmed while another is skipped, so the record is only partly validated. Scored 2 because identification was attempted and the call was not handled on a wholly unverified basis.
pass_example: Agent takes both the customer's name and the exact area or street before opening the record and proceeding.

attr_definition: Correctly establishing who the caller is and which account, meter or location the enquiry relates to. Covers capturing every identifier required by the Runaki process (name, area/address, contact number, subscriber/meter or complaint reference), working in the correct record, and reading details back for confirmation before acting on them.
reason: Worked from the wrong account / incorrect information
definition: The agent opened, updated or advised on a record that does not belong to the caller, or used details (meter number, address, phone number) that do not match the customer. Everything the agent says from that point is unreliable.
pass_example: "I have two registrations under this name - is yours the one in Shorsh or the one in Zanko?" Agent confirms before reading anything out.

attr_definition: Correctly establishing who the caller is and which account, meter or location the enquiry relates to. Covers capturing every identifier required by the Runaki process (name, area/address, contact number, subscriber/meter or complaint reference), working in the correct record, and reading details back for confirmation before acting on them.
reason: Did not confirm details back to the customer accurately
definition: Details were collected but never repeated back, or were repeated back incorrectly and the error was left uncorrected, so there is no verbal check that what was entered matches what the customer said.
pass_example: "Let me read that back to you: 0750 123 4567, Erbil, Bakhtiary district. Is that correct?"

attr_definition: Correctly establishing who the caller is and which account, meter or location the enquiry relates to. Covers capturing every identifier required by the Runaki process (name, area/address, contact number, subscriber/meter or complaint reference), working in the correct record, and reading details back for confirmation before acting on them.
reason: Did not confirm all required customer information
definition: One or more mandatory fields in the Runaki identification set were never requested at all, so the case is logged incomplete and cannot be actioned or followed up properly.
pass_example: Agent captures every mandatory field before closing: name, callback number, exact area/address, and the Account number or complaint reference.

attr_definition: Whether the agent lets the customer explain the issue in full, audibly signals attention while they speak, and confirms understanding by paraphrasing the issue back before offering a solution, so the customer never has to repeat information already given.
reason: Pass
definition: Full pass. The customer explains the issue without being cut off, the agent signals attention throughout, and the issue is paraphrased back and confirmed before any solution is offered.
pass_example: Customer describes a three-day outage; agent responds "I understand - so the power on your street has been off since Friday evening and your neighbours are affected too. Let me check what is logged for that area."

attr_definition: Whether the agent lets the customer explain the issue in full, audibly signals attention while they speak, and confirms understanding by paraphrasing the issue back before offering a solution, so the customer never has to repeat information already given.
reason: Interrupted or spoke over the customer
definition: The agent cuts across the customer while they are still explaining - talking over them, finishing their sentences, or answering a question they have not yet asked. A single overlap caused by line delay is not scored; repeated or dismissive interruption is.
pass_example: Agent waits for a natural pause before asking the clarifying question, even when the answer is already obvious to them.

attr_definition: Whether the agent lets the customer explain the issue in full, audibly signals attention while they speak, and confirms understanding by paraphrasing the issue back before offering a solution, so the customer never has to repeat information already given.
reason: Did not acknowledge the customer's concern (no verbal nods / empathy statements)
definition: The agent processes the request mechanically with no verbal acknowledgement or empathy marker, so the customer receives silence or bare functional prompts while describing a problem that is affecting them.
pass_example: "I am sorry you have been without power for three days, that must be very difficult. Let me look at this for you now."

attr_definition: Whether the agent lets the customer explain the issue in full, audibly signals attention while they speak, and confirms understanding by paraphrasing the issue back before offering a solution, so the customer never has to repeat information already given.
reason: Did not paraphrase or confirm understanding of the issue
definition: The agent never restates the issue in their own words, so there is no evidence on the call that the request was understood correctly before action was taken or the call was closed.
pass_example: "So to confirm - you registered last month, you have not received the confirmation SMS, and you want to know the status of the Registartion."

attr_definition: Whether the agent lets the customer explain the issue in full, audibly signals attention while they speak, and confirms understanding by paraphrasing the issue back before offering a solution, so the customer never has to repeat information already given.
reason: Did not demonstrate attention — customer had to repeat themselves
definition: The customer is required to give the same information again because the agent was not attending - asking for a detail already provided, or asking the customer to start their explanation over.
pass_example: Agent captures the details on first hearing and refers back to them accurately later in the call.

attr_definition: Whether the information given matches the approved Runaki FAQ / knowledge base - accurate, current and sufficiently complete - and whether queries falling outside the agent's authorised scope are escalated rather than answered from personal judgement.
reason: Pass
definition: Full pass. The answer is accurate, matches the current approved knowledge base, and covers what the customer needs; anything outside the agent's scope is escalated through the correct route.
pass_example: Customer asks how the tariff blocks are calculated; the agent gives the approved FAQ explanation in full and checks the customer has understood it.

attr_definition: Whether the information given matches the approved Runaki FAQ / knowledge base - accurate, current and sufficiently complete - and whether queries falling outside the agent's authorised scope are escalated rather than answered from personal judgement.
reason: Provided the correct answer, but could have been more comprehensive.
definition: Substantively correct and not misleading, but thin. A relevant condition, next step, or related detail from the same FAQ entry was left out, and the customer may need to call again to get it. Scored 2.
pass_example: Agent states the outcome, the expected timeframe(Confirmed by the client), what the customer will receive, and what to do if it does not arrive.

attr_definition: Whether the information given matches the approved Runaki FAQ / knowledge base - accurate, current and sufficiently complete - and whether queries falling outside the agent's authorised scope are escalated rather than answered from personal judgement.
reason: Gave incorrect or misleading information (CRITICAL)
definition: The agent stated something factually wrong or likely to mislead - a wrong amount, wrong timeframe, wrong procedure, or a commitment Runaki does not make. Marked CRITICAL because it exposes both the customer and the client to a wrong outcome and commonly generates a complaint.
pass_example: Agent checks the FAQ or the system before answering and gives only the confirmed figure or procedure.

attr_definition: Whether the information given matches the approved Runaki FAQ / knowledge base - accurate, current and sufficiently complete - and whether queries falling outside the agent's authorised scope are escalated rather than answered from personal judgement.
reason: Did not escalate when the query fell outside FAQ scope
definition: The query fell outside what the agent is authorised to answer and should have been transferred, logged for escalation or referred to the Ministry route, but the agent answered it anyway or simply closed it.
pass_example: "That decision sits with the CO team. I will log this and escalate it so they can come back to you."

attr_definition: Whether the information given matches the approved Runaki FAQ / knowledge base - accurate, current and sufficiently complete - and whether queries falling outside the agent's authorised scope are escalated rather than answered from personal judgement.
reason: Response did not match the approved FAQ / knowledge base
definition: The information is not necessarily wrong on its face, but it is the agent's own wording or a superseded version rather than the current approved content - producing inconsistent answers across the team.
pass_example: Agent delivers the current approved wording for the registration process as published in the knowledge base.

attr_definition: How clearly the message is delivered: language quality and professional register, articulation and pace, and a structured answer free of unnecessary repetition or filler, in the customer's chosen language.
reason: Pass
definition: Full pass. Clear, well-paced, professional delivery in the customer's language; the customer understands the answer the first time and does not need it repeated.
pass_example: Agent explains the complaint process in short, ordered steps at a steady pace, then checks "Is that clear so far?"

attr_definition: How clearly the message is delivered: language quality and professional register, articulation and pace, and a structured answer free of unnecessary repetition or filler, in the customer's chosen language.
reason: Response was clear and appropriate but could have been delivered more effectively
definition: The customer received correct information, but the delivery was clumsy - poor structure, hesitation, over-long sentences, or the key point buried at the end. Understanding was still achieved, so this scores 2.
pass_example: Agent leads with the answer, then gives the reason, then the next step.

attr_definition: How clearly the message is delivered: language quality and professional register, articulation and pace, and a structured answer free of unnecessary repetition or filler, in the customer's chosen language.
reason: Grammar errors or unprofessional language used
definition: Language errors serious enough to affect meaning or credibility, heavy use of filler words, slang, or casual expressions unsuited to a Ministry-facing service, in any of the three call languages.
pass_example: Agent maintains a correct, formal register throughout in Arabic, Sorani or Badini.

attr_definition: How clearly the message is delivered: language quality and professional register, articulation and pace, and a structured answer free of unnecessary repetition or filler, in the customer's chosen language.
reason: Unnecessary repetition throughout the call
definition: The agent repeats the same information, question or script line several times with no new value, extending handling time and frustrating the customer.
pass_example: Information is given once, clearly, and confirmed once at the close.

attr_definition: How clearly the message is delivered: language quality and professional register, articulation and pace, and a structured answer free of unnecessary repetition or filler, in the customer's chosen language.
reason: Unclear articulation or inappropriate pace
definition: Mumbling, trailing off, speaking too fast to follow, or so slowly the customer disengages; also covers speaking away from the microphone so the customer cannot hear clearly.
pass_example: Reference numbers and figures are given slowly and digit by digit; the rest of the call at normal conversational pace.

attr_definition: Whether the agent identifies the actual cause of the customer's issue and resolves it through the correct Runaki process - achieving first-contact resolution where the issue is within scope, and correct escalation where it is not.
reason: Pass
definition: Full pass. The root cause is correctly identified, an appropriate solution is applied through the correct process, and the outcome or next step is clear to the customer before the call ends.
pass_example: Customer is not receiving messages; agent checks the system and identifies that the messages are being sent to another registered mobile number, then follows the correct process to address the issue and clearly explains the outcome to the customer.

attr_definition: Whether the agent identifies the actual cause of the customer's issue and resolves it through the correct Runaki process - achieving first-contact resolution where the issue is within scope, and correct escalation where it is not.
reason: Identified the issue and provided a solution, but the resolution was not fully effective
definition: The agent diagnosed correctly and acted, but the resolution was incomplete - a step left to the customer unnecessarily, a partial fix, or an outcome likely to generate a repeat call. Scored 2.
pass_example: Agent completes every step within their authority before closing, so no further customer action is needed.

attr_definition: Whether the agent identifies the actual cause of the customer's issue and resolves it through the correct Runaki process - achieving first-contact resolution where the issue is within scope, and correct escalation where it is not.
reason: Did not identify the root cause of the issue
definition: The agent treated the surface symptom without establishing what caused it - no probing questions, no check of the record - so the answer may not address the customer's real problem.
pass_example: Agent confirms whether the full neighbourhood is affected or only the customer, then checks the CRM for dunning information before proceeding with the appropriate handling.

attr_definition: Whether the agent identifies the actual cause of the customer's issue and resolves it through the correct Runaki process - achieving first-contact resolution where the issue is within scope, and correct escalation where it is not.
reason: Solution offered was not appropriate to the problem (CRITICAL)
definition: The action or advice given does not fit the issue - wrong department, wrong procedure, or advice that cannot resolve the customer's situation. CRITICAL because the customer leaves the call believing the matter is handled when it is not.
pass_example: A meter fault is raised as a technical work order to the field team, which is the route that can actually resolve it.

attr_definition: Whether the agent identifies the actual cause of the customer's issue and resolves it through the correct Runaki process - achieving first-contact resolution where the issue is within scope, and correct escalation where it is not.
reason: Did not follow the correct process
definition: A resolution was reached but the defined Runaki workflow was bypassed - no ticket raised, wrong escalation route, a mandatory step skipped, or an undertaking given outside the agent's authority.
pass_example: Agent follows the escalation matrix and records the case in the system before ending the call.

attr_definition: Accuracy and completeness of after-call work: selecting the tag, sub-category and disposition that match the customer's stated reason for contact and the true outcome, and leaving notes clear enough for a colleague or the client to understand the case without listening to the call.
reason: Pass
definition: Full pass. The tag and sub-category match the customer's reason for contact, the disposition reflects the true outcome, and the notes are clear enough to be used by the next person who reads the record.
pass_example: An area outage in Ainkawa is tagged Complaint > Power Outage > Area-wide, with a note recording the street, the duration, and the reference given to the customer.

attr_definition: Accuracy and completeness of after-call work: selecting the tag, sub-category and disposition that match the customer's stated reason for contact and the true outcome, and leaving notes clear enough for a colleague or the client to understand the case without listening to the call.
reason: Tag / topic was generally appropriate but could have been more accurate based on the call content
definition: The main category is correct but the sub-category or level of detail does not fully reflect the call, where a more precise option existed. Reporting remains broadly usable, so this scores 2.
pass_example: Agent selects the specific sub-category rather than stopping at the parent category.

attr_definition: Accuracy and completeness of after-call work: selecting the tag, sub-category and disposition that match the customer's stated reason for contact and the true outcome, and leaving notes clear enough for a colleague or the client to understand the case without listening to the call.
reason: Call tagged with the wrong topic / category (CRITICAL)
definition: The tag does not reflect the reason for contact at all. CRITICAL because it corrupts the client-facing reporting Runaki uses to direct field and Ministry action, and because the error is invisible once the call has aged.
pass_example: A complaint is tagged as a complaint, not downgraded to an enquiry.

attr_definition: Accuracy and completeness of after-call work: selecting the tag, sub-category and disposition that match the customer's stated reason for contact and the true outcome, and leaving notes clear enough for a colleague or the client to understand the case without listening to the call.
reason: Disposition code did not match actual call content
definition: The outcome code contradicts what actually happened - for example marked resolved when it was escalated, or marked escalated when nothing was raised in the system.
pass_example: A call escalated to the field team is dispositioned "Escalated - Pending".

attr_definition: Accuracy and completeness of after-call work: selecting the tag, sub-category and disposition that match the customer's stated reason for contact and the true outcome, and leaving notes clear enough for a colleague or the client to understand the case without listening to the call.
reason: Notes not logged clearly for future reference
definition: Notes are missing, too brief, ambiguous or unreadable, so a colleague or the client cannot reconstruct what the customer wanted and what was done without listening to the recording.
pass_example: Customer reported having no electricity supply since 12/06. Agent checked the case and found that a work order for disconnection due to non-payment had been raised, then provided the Correct Time frame for reconnection after payment to the customer.

attr_definition: Accuracy and completeness of after-call work: selecting the tag, sub-category and disposition that match the customer's stated reason for contact and the true outcome, and leaving notes clear enough for a colleague or the client to understand the case without listening to the call.
reason: Tag not applied based on the customer's reason for contact
definition: The tag was chosen from what the agent did, or from habit or the default selection, rather than from why the customer called - including leaving the pre-selected tag untouched.
pass_example: Agent tags on the customer's stated reason for contact even where the call was resolved with a simple piece of information.

attr_definition: The attitude the customer hears: professional courtesy sustained from open to close, empathy proportionate to the situation, and positive phrasing that tells the customer what can be done rather than only what cannot.
reason: Pass
definition: Full pass. Courteous, calm and engaged from open to close, with empathy where the situation warrants it and positive language even when the answer is no.
pass_example: "I understand how difficult this is in this heat. I cannot restore the supply from here, but what I can do is escalate it now as a priority fault."

attr_definition: The attitude the customer hears: professional courtesy sustained from open to close, empathy proportionate to the situation, and positive phrasing that tells the customer what can be done rather than only what cannot.
reason: Maintained an appropriate tone, but could have been more positive, empathetic, or engaging
definition: Nothing rude or unprofessional, but the tone was neutral and transactional where a degree of warmth or acknowledgement was called for. Scored 2.
pass_example: Agent adds a brief empathy statement before moving into the process steps.

attr_definition: The attitude the customer hears: professional courtesy sustained from open to close, empathy proportionate to the situation, and positive phrasing that tells the customer what can be done rather than only what cannot.
reason: Did not maintain a professional, courteous tone throughout
definition: Tone deteriorated at some point during the call - impatience, sighing, abruptness or audible irritation - even where the opening was handled well.
pass_example: The tone at minute eight is the same as the tone at minute one.

attr_definition: The attitude the customer hears: professional courtesy sustained from open to close, empathy proportionate to the situation, and positive phrasing that tells the customer what can be done rather than only what cannot.
reason: Did not display empathy appropriate to the situation
definition: The situation clearly warranted acknowledgement - a vulnerable household, a long outage, repeated failed contact - and the agent gave none, or gave a scripted line with no relevance to what was described.
pass_example: "I am sorry - I can see this is the third time you have called about this. Let me make sure it is escalated properly this time."

attr_definition: The attitude the customer hears: professional courtesy sustained from open to close, empathy proportionate to the situation, and positive phrasing that tells the customer what can be done rather than only what cannot.
reason: Used negative phrasing instead of positive language
definition: The agent frames the answer around refusal, blame or limitation - "you cannot", "that is not my job", "nothing can be done" - where an approved positive alternative exists.
pass_example: "What I can do is log this now and give you the reference so you can follow it up."

attr_definition: The attitude the customer hears: professional courtesy sustained from open to close, empathy proportionate to the situation, and positive phrasing that tells the customer what can be done rather than only what cannot.
reason: Did not maintain a helpful and positive attitude
definition: The agent is technically compliant but audibly unwilling - reluctant, minimum-effort responses that signal the customer is an inconvenience.
pass_example: Agent volunteers an extra check without being asked: "Let me also confirm whether the work order has been assigned yet."

attr_definition: How the call is closed: summary of the resolution or next steps, the approved closing and further-assistance script, the mandatory KYC verification wording, and a courteous confirmation that the customer has everything they need.
reason: Pass
definition: Full pass. The resolution or next steps are summarised, further assistance is offered, the required KYC verification wording is delivered, and the customer is thanked using the approved closing.
pass_example: I have recorded the issue and the necessary process has been followed. Please wait for further updates regarding your case. Is there anything else I can help you with today?.

attr_definition: How the call is closed: summary of the resolution or next steps, the approved closing and further-assistance script, the mandatory KYC verification wording, and a courteous confirmation that the customer has everything they need.
reason: Provided an appropriate closing, but some elements of the ending were incomplete
definition: The call was closed courteously but one component of the required close was missing or rushed - for example a summary given without the offer of further assistance. Scored 2.
pass_example: All required elements are present: summary, offer of further assistance, verification wording, and thanks.

attr_definition: How the call is closed: summary of the resolution or next steps, the approved closing and further-assistance script, the mandatory KYC verification wording, and a courteous confirmation that the customer has everything they need.
reason: Did not use the approved closing script + further-assistance script
definition: The mandated closing wording and the "is there anything else" question were not used, so the call ends without the standard Runaki close.
pass_example: Agent delivers both the further-assistance question and the approved closing line in full.

attr_definition: How the call is closed: summary of the resolution or next steps, the approved closing and further-assistance script, the mandatory KYC verification wording, and a courteous confirmation that the customer has everything they need.
reason: Did not summarise the resolution / next steps
definition: The customer is left without a clear statement of what was decided, what happens next, by when, and which reference to quote.
pass_example: "To summarise: the meter reading has been corrected, and the adjusted amount will appear on your next bill."

attr_definition: How the call is closed: summary of the resolution or next steps, the approved closing and further-assistance script, the mandatory KYC verification wording, and a courteous confirmation that the customer has everything they need.
reason: Did not thank the customer or confirm satisfaction
definition: The call ends with no thanks and no check that the customer's need was actually met.
pass_example: "Have I answered everything for you today? Thank you for calling Runaki."

attr_definition: How the call is closed: summary of the resolution or next steps, the approved closing and further-assistance script, the mandatory KYC verification wording, and a courteous confirmation that the customer has everything they need.
reason: Did not mention the KYC verification script (CRITICAL)
definition: The mandatory KYC / verification wording required at the close of every Runaki inbound call was omitted. CRITICAL because it is a client compliance requirement and its absence is auditable, regardless of how well the rest of the call was handled.
pass_example: Agent delivers the KYC verification wording in full before the closing line.

attr_definition: Zero-tolerance conduct check. Whether the agent remained respectful and composed at all times, with no rudeness, dismissiveness, sarcasm or argument, regardless of how difficult or provocative the customer is.
reason: Pass
definition: Full pass. No disrespect, sarcasm, argument or loss of patience at any point; the agent stays calm and respectful even under provocation.
pass_example: Customer swears in frustration; agent stays level: "I understand you are angry. I am here to help - let me check this for you now."

attr_definition: Zero-tolerance conduct check. Whether the agent remained respectful and composed at all times, with no rudeness, dismissiveness, sarcasm or argument, regardless of how difficult or provocative the customer is.
reason: Used disrespectful, dismissive or rude language (CRITICAL)
definition: Any insult, mockery, blame directed at the customer, raised voice, or dismissive statement. CRITICAL - a single instance fails the attribute and should trigger immediate coaching and, where warranted, escalation to management or HR.
pass_example: Agent disagrees respectfully: "I understand your view. Let me explain what the system is showing me."

attr_definition: Zero-tolerance conduct check. Whether the agent remained respectful and composed at all times, with no rudeness, dismissiveness, sarcasm or argument, regardless of how difficult or provocative the customer is.
reason: Did not remain patient under pressure
definition: The agent lost composure with a difficult, repetitive or angry customer - arguing back, talking over them in frustration, or audibly giving up - short of outright rudeness.
pass_example: Customer asks the same question five times; the agent answers each time with the same calm wording.

attr_definition: Zero-tolerance conduct check. Whether the agent remained respectful and composed at all times, with no rudeness, dismissiveness, sarcasm or argument, regardless of how difficult or provocative the customer is.
reason: Inappropriate tone / sarcasm directed at the customer
definition: The words would read as acceptable in a transcript but the delivery is not: sarcasm, mocking repetition, laughing at the customer, or an exaggerated tone that belittles them.
pass_example: Sincere, level delivery with no edge, even when the customer's request is unreasonable.

attr_definition: Whether the call was terminated correctly - released only after the customer confirmed they had nothing further, following the defined disconnection and wrap-up procedure, with no premature or abrupt drop.
reason: Pass
definition: Full pass. The line is released only after the customer has confirmed they need nothing further, and in line with the defined disconnection and wrap-up procedure.
pass_example: Agent asks whether anything further is needed, the customer says no, the agent closes properly and disconnect the call.

attr_definition: Whether the call was terminated correctly - released only after the customer confirmed they had nothing further, following the defined disconnection and wrap-up procedure, with no premature or abrupt drop.
reason: Disconnected the call prematurely (CRITICAL)
definition: The agent released the call while the customer was still speaking, or before their issue was addressed, including deliberate drops of difficult calls. CRITICAL - treated as call avoidance and investigated as a conduct matter.
pass_example: Even where the customer is abusive, the agent follows the approved warn-and-terminate procedure before disconnecting.

attr_definition: Whether the call was terminated correctly - released only after the customer confirmed they had nothing further, following the defined disconnection and wrap-up procedure, with no premature or abrupt drop.
reason: Ended the call without customer confirmation
definition: The agent closed the call without asking, or without waiting for, the customer's confirmation that they had nothing further, so the customer's agreement to end was never obtained.
pass_example: "Is there anything else before I close the call?" - and the agent waits for the answer.

attr_definition: Whether the call was terminated correctly - released only after the customer confirmed they had nothing further, following the defined disconnection and wrap-up procedure, with no premature or abrupt drop.
reason: Call closure did not follow proper procedure
definition: The disconnection itself breached procedure - dropping instead of transferring, releasing before required wrap-up or notes were completed, or leaving the customer on hold until the line timed out.
pass_example: Agent completes wrap-up and disposition, then releases the call in line with procedure.
